title: Open WebUI legacy chat completions -- T1548 client-supplied features flag bypasses the revoked image-generation permission
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-70484 (GHSA-g423-grf7-98rv,
CVSS 4.3 MEDIUM), affecting Open WebUI's legacy chat-completions
path.

The two direct image routes (`/images/generations`, `/images/edit`)
and the native function-calling path all re-check the caller's
`features.image_generation` permission before reaching an image
provider. The legacy chat-completions path -- reached by setting
`params.function_calling` to `legacy` -- does not: it stores the
request's client-supplied `features` object into request metadata and
`process_chat_payload` dispatches to the image handler purely on that
flag's truthiness, never re-checking it against the caller's actual
permission. A user an administrator has explicitly revoked image
generation from can still trigger it by sending
`features.image_generation: true` on a legacy chat-completions
request, spending the operator's provider credits and quota.

Detection logic flags a chat-completions request body carrying
`features.image_generation: true` together with legacy function-
calling mode -- the exact unchecked-flag combination this advisory
describes.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (open-webui, via
GHSA and NVD, citing the exact commit and PR), fixed in commit
`897d69a` (PR #26703).
